500	we learn to prepare the table and arrange the meal,
501	even though it was made for the use of others.
502	How can we know what the inner will of
503	the carpenter and the cook was?

510	the table or from the meal. Yitzhak Liberman:
511	Why must the teaching of Kabbalah be hidden? After all, today when we come to speak of
512	the desire to receive and the desire to bestow, people run away
513	from it. Without building a vessel one cannot receive light. What is the great
514	secret that they did not want to reveal? Answer:
515	They did not want to reveal what Judaism truly is. Only over the course of
516	the generations there is such a blurring
517	that people think they hold on to Judaism and do not know what
518	true Judaism is. Now our Rabbi,
519	Baal HaSulam, revealed, not everything, but he revealed large parts
520	of Judaism. So it is not only the desire to receive and the desire to bestow,
521	but it carries implications for all of Judaism: what
522	the Torah is, what the explanations in the Torah are, what the mitzvot are. Certainly
523	regarding the wisdom of Kabbalah, as it is learned without Baal HaSulam,
524	it is a kind of plumbing system with pipes and valves
525	going up and down, pumps, and he comes and introduces here
526	the dimension of the soul, the psychological, the heart.
527	He links this with Chassidut. All this was hidden; today he
528	revealed it. That does not mean it is accessible to everyone, and therefore there really is
529	great opposition, because there are people for whom this simply dismantles
530	everything they were accustomed to, and places them in a very, very
531	ridiculous, small and lowly light. So there is great opposition to this
532	matter. But in any case he opened these matters to that part
533	of the public, even if it is only two, three percent
534	of the whole public, five percent, then it was already worthwhile.
535	Raanan: is there a connection between the revelation of the teaching of Kabbalah
536	and the development of the freedom we see today, which crosses
537	every boundary?
538	There is a connection.
539	"The one opposite the other Elokim has made": holiness opposite impurity.
540	So the revelation of the foundations of holiness, which depend greatly
541	on restriction and a screen over the mind and over the heart of the person,
542	causes the other side, that of impurity, to seek to dismantle
543	all the restrictions and all the laws and all the screens, so that each man
544	does what is right in his own eyes, like the beasts and animals of the field,
545	and they call it humanism.
546	Humanism.
547	Why is it called humanism?
548	The freedom of the individual.
549	More questions. Gadi Gever:
550	In the synagogues, the subject of the inner Torah and Kabbalah is not popular,
551	to put it mildly.
552	And as worshippers we also keep a very low profile
553	on the matter of the inner dimension.
554	What does the Rabbi recommend on this subject
555	in the synagogues?
556	Look, everything depends, and everything is judged on its own merits.
557	That is, if for example you come to a Haredi synagogue
558	and try to start selling them
559	the foundations of the wisdom of Kabbalah, they look down on you:

562	teshuvah, not with their noses in the air and so on, people who regard themselves
563	as simple people, you can try to give
564	them some small pamphlet, a few pages,
565	to see whether it interests them or not, without much talk.
566	You give the person some small pamphlet, such as for example
567	the second chapter of the book Bilvav Shalem, where there are
568	the foundations of the method, the method of Baal HaSulam.
569	You give the person this pamphlet, I know it is thirty pages,
570	you tell him: listen, see whether it interests you or not, without much talk.
571	Interesting, interesting? If it interests him, then give him the whole book Bilvav
572	Shalem.
573	If it doesn't interest him, then all the best, goodbye.

575	of Baal HaSulam?

577	They don't know them and they don't accept them.

511	Por que é preciso ocultar o ensinamento da Cabalá? Afinal, hoje, quando vamos falar do
512	desejo de receber e do desejo de doar, as pessoas fogem
513	disso. Sem construir um vaso não se pode receber luz. Qual é o grande
514	segredo que não quiseram revelar? Resposta:
515	Não quiseram revelar o que realmente é o judaísmo. Só ao longo
516	das gerações há um tal embaçamento
517	que as pessoas pensam que se apegam ao judaísmo e não sabem qual é
518	o verdadeiro judaísmo. Agora, nosso Rabino,
519	Baal HaSulam, revelou, não tudo, mas revelou grandes partes
520	do judaísmo. Então não é só o desejo de receber e o desejo de doar,
521	mas isso traz implicações para todo o judaísmo: o que
522	é a Torá, quais são as explicações na Torá, o que são as mitsvot. Certamente
523	quanto à sabedoria da Cabalá, como se estuda sem Baal HaSulam,
524	é uma espécie de sistema hidráulico com canos e válvulas
525	que sobem e descem, bombas, e ele vem e introduz aqui
526	a dimensão da alma, a psicológica, a do coração.
527	Ele liga isso com o Chassidut. Tudo isso estava oculto; hoje ele
528	revelou. Isso não quer dizer que seja acessível a todos, e por isso realmente há
529	grande oposição, porque há pessoas para quem isso simplesmente desmonta
530	tudo a que estavam habituadas, e as coloca numa luz muito, muito
531	ridícula, pequena e baixa. Por isso há grande oposição a isso.
532	Mas, de qualquer modo, ele abriu essas coisas para aquela parte
533	do público, mesmo que sejam só dois, três por cento
534	de todo o público, cinco por cento, então já valeu a pena.

541	da restrição e de um anteparo sobre a mente e sobre o coração do ser humano,
